messages.server.save_target: Saved to the working copy when there is one, otherwise to the published file.

messages.error.bad_request: The request has the wrong shape.
messages.error.bad_utf8: The text arrived corrupted. Nothing was written.
messages.error.conflict: The file changed underneath. Nothing was written.
messages.error.save_failed: Could not save. The file was not changed.
messages.error.save_check_failed: A row did not read back as written in the check before writing, so nothing was written. The other rows are saved when sent again.
messages.error.file_readonly: This file is read-only. It cannot be saved.
messages.error.no_row_saved: Not one row could be saved.
messages.error.row_moved: This row has shifted. A different key now sits in that position, so nothing was written. Please reload.
messages.error.unknown_form: That is not a form this can write out.
messages.error.export_failed: Could not write it out. No file was made.
messages.error.export_would_lose: Writing this form out would leave {count} translations from the committed file out of the new output. Not a byte was written. This happens when committed rows are missing from the working copy (the "dropped by publish" count on screen looks at the working copy instead, so it can stay at 0). A working copy lists only the rows whose text the game has loaded at least once. If the missing rows are mod or settings screens, open those screens in the game once, then press F1 (the default) then Translation then Export working copy to make the working copy again. Run dwloc publish to see which rows.
messages.error.export_unsafe_shape: Nothing was written out: the file has a shape that is misread ({count} places). The header lacks a key or translation column (it has neither key nor source_en, it has no translation, or its first column name starts with '#'), a quote is never closed, a quote is closed on another line and swallows the lines after it into a value, a value contains a lone CR, an unquoted value is cut by a lone CR, the line breaks are misread so that not a single row can be read, or a value of the play order data that is written as is, such as into a heading, contains a line break. dwloc publish shows which file and line, and how to fix it. If it stops on a correct multi-line value, check it and write it with dwloc publish --accept-multiline <locale>:<key>, once for each record (dwloc publish prints the option to copy when it stops).
messages.error.export_would_roll_back: The translations installed in the game are older, so nothing was written out. {count} translations differ between the game and the committed file. The working copy carries those older translations, so writing this form out would roll back newer commits. Put the latest translations into the game, then make the working copy again.
messages.warn.value_normalized: The saved value differs from what you typed. The value in the file is shown.
messages.ui.edit_notice: Pick a translation cell to edit it. It is saved when you stop typing. publish is not run. What you typed stays even after the input closes.
messages.ui.save_failed_detail: Could not save. Your translations stay on screen and are sent again automatically after a short wait. Reloading drops any that have not been sent yet.
messages.ui.discard_confirm: Some translations are not saved. Reloading drops them. Reload anyway?
messages.ui.switch_confirm: Some translations are not saved. Switching the locale drops them. Switch anyway?
messages.ui.conflict_title: The file changed underneath. Your edits are kept.
messages.ui.conflict_help: What was re-read is shown below. Pick which one to keep. Auto-save is paused until you pick. This choice covers only the rows below that show both "In the file" and "Yours". What you type on any other row is kept either way.
messages.ui.conflict_take_file: Take what is in the file
messages.ui.conflict_locked: Choose which one to keep before editing this row.
messages.ui.orphans_title: Some translations no longer have a row to go to. The row left the file, more rows now share its key, or the row can no longer be edited. Copy them down, then reload.
messages.ui.unreachable: Cannot reach the server. If dwloc has stopped (it stops by itself after a while with no activity), start it again and open the new URL shown in the black window.
messages.ui.save_refused: The server does not accept saves from this screen ({status}). Waiting will not fix it, so it is not retried automatically. If you restarted dwloc, open the new URL shown in the black window.
messages.ui.unsent_title: These translations are not in the file yet. Note them down before you move to the new URL or close this screen. On the new screen, typing the key into the search box brings up the row.
messages.ui.game_folder: Game folder searched for working copies
messages.note.via_publish: What you see is a working copy. Saving writes to this file only. Your translations reach {path}, the file you commit, when you run dwloc publish.
messages.note.no_source: There is no working copy, so the source column stays empty.
messages.ui.export_help: Save the CSV for the locale you have open to any place you like. The browser asks where it goes. Saving here does not change where this editor normally saves. If you have unsaved translations, wait until they are sent, then press.
messages.ui.export_published_note: The same form dwloc publish makes. Keys become hashes and rows follow the script order. You can drop it straight into the repository.
messages.ui.export_working: Save the file you are editing, as it is
messages.ui.export_working_note: A plain copy of the file being written to: the working copy when there is one, the published file itself when there is not.
messages.ui.export_wait: Unsaved translations are being sent. Press again once that is done.
messages.ui.export_conflict: There is a conflict. Pick which translation to keep, then press again.
messages.ui.export_row_failed: Some rows could not be saved. Fix them using the reason shown on each row, then press again.
messages.ui.export_orphans: Some translations have no row to go to. Copy them down and reload, then press again.
messages.ui.filter: Filter (numbers are rows in this list)
messages.ui.no_rows: No row matches. Clear the conditions to see them all.
messages.ui.no_rows_search: No row contains what you typed. Empty the search box to bring the rows back.
messages.ui.finder_note_title: About filtering and search (search runs inside your browser only)
messages.ui.finder_note: Pick as many conditions as you like; a row is shown when it matches any of them. The bracketed number on a chip is how many rows in the list as it stands match that condition. Picking two conditions does not add the two numbers up. Only "showing" in the top bar says how many rows are on screen right now. The number on a chip and the number of rows on screen come apart in three ways. First, saving a translation takes that condition's badge off the row and lowers the number, but the list itself is left as it is, so that rows do not vanish from under you while you type. Second, rows with unsaved translations, rows that could not be saved, and the row whose input is open right now are never hidden, so more rows can be on screen than the number says. Third, what you type in the search box is not counted, so typing leaves fewer rows on screen. Search runs inside the browser only, so what you type reaches neither the server nor the URL; that is the same reason it is not counted. Closing the input hides that row again if it does not match (while you work down the rows with Enter it stays, because it is not saved yet). Where the number in Counts (found by the check at startup) differs from the number of rows this list can show, Counts says so on that line. Some categories cannot be shown as rows at all, for example when the row is not in this locale's file; their chips say so instead of showing a number.
messages.ui.keys_help: In a translation cell, Enter commits and opens the next row. Escape only closes the input. Tab also moves to the next row. Press slash outside an input to jump to the search box. Keys are never taken over while composing. The Enter that commits a composition is not used to advance either, so that committing alone never jumps to the next row. On the last row shown, Enter keeps the input open and stays there. On a narrow screen, slash opens the side column first. The locale box loads a moment after you choose, so moving through it with the arrow keys only loads the locale you stop on. To open the list before choosing, press Alt+Down.
messages.note.counts_local: Counts come from the check at startup. Rows you translated are subtracted from Untranslated, and the tag balance of rows you saved is re-checked, but no other category is re-judged. Restart dwloc edit to recount.
messages.note.working_none: No working copy ({path}). Untranslated rows and rows dropped by publish cannot be judged.
messages.note.working_skipped: The working copy was not read ({path}).
messages.note.order_unreadable: The play order could not be read. Rows gone from the script are not judged.
messages.note.order_line_ids_missing: The play order has no line IDs (line_id). {categories} are not judged.
messages.note.order_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the play order (data/script_order.csv) is never closed before the end of the file, so the play order cannot be read. No category is judged.
messages.note.published_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the published file ({path}) is never closed before the end of the file, so it cannot be read. No category is judged for this locale.
messages.note.working_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the working copy ({path}) is never closed before the end of the file, so it cannot be read. Untranslated rows, rows dropped by publish and others are not judged.
messages.note.layout_risks_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the overflow record ({path}) is never closed before the end of the file, so it cannot be read.
messages.note.old_order_held: Carry-over candidates are not judged ({reason}). No rows here does not mean there is nowhere to carry a translation to.

messages.category.locale_gap: Missing here but present in another locale
messages.category.stray_line_id: Line-ID row not in the script
messages.category.script_gap: Dialogue row not in the script
messages.category.tag_mismatch: Rows whose tags differ from the source

messages.reason.judge_order_no_line_ids: The play order has no line IDs (line_id)
messages.reason.judge_order_no_norms: The play order has no norm column

messages.reason.judge_layout_risks_not_read: The overflow record was not read

messages.reason.judge_order_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the play order is never closed
messages.reason.judge_published_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the published file is never closed
messages.reason.judge_working_unclosed: The quote opened on line {line} of the working copy is never closed

messages.reason.judge_other_published_unclosed: A quote in the published file of another locale ({locales}) is never closed
messages.reason.old_order_no_repository: Not a git repository, or it has no commits
messages.reason.old_order_not_tracked: The play order is not tracked by git
messages.reason.old_order_not_committed: The play order has not been committed yet
messages.reason.old_order_only_one_version: The play order has only one version in its history
messages.reason.old_order_git_failed: git could not produce the previous play order
messages.reason.old_order_unreadable: The previous play order could not be parsed
messages.reason.old_order_no_line_ids: The previous play order has no line ID and key pairs
messages.reason.old_order_stale: The previous play order that was read looks the same as the current one
messages.reason.note_vanished: It was in the play order at the last publish
messages.reason.note_stray_line_id: No row in the play order has this line ID
messages.reason.note_not_published: No locale has a translation for it
messages.reason.note_unknown_origin: Not in the play order, but it may be UI text
messages.reason.note_dropped_broken: key is neither 16 hex digits nor a line: value
messages.reason.note_dropped_mismatch: The hash of source_en does not match key
messages.reason.note_dropped_source_crlf: The line breaks in source_en are CRLF. Turned back into LF, it matches key
messages.reason.note_carry_moved: Carry over to {target} (moved: the old key has left the play order)
messages.reason.note_carry_copied: Carry over to {target} (copied: the old key is still live at {live}, so keep the translation on this row)
messages.reason.note_carry_from_same: Carry over from {source} (the source text differs only in formatting and punctuation)
messages.reason.note_carry_from_similar: Carry over from {source} (the source text was rewritten; fingerprint distance {distance}; check it before you use it)
messages.reason.note_carry_copied_unknown: Carry over to {target} (copied: the old key is still live on another row, so keep the translation on this row)
messages.reason.note_tag_unclosed_unopened: Unclosed tags: {unclosed} / closing tags without an opening: {unopened}
messages.reason.note_layout_risk: May overflow (ratio {ratio}, {axis} axis, needs {required} of {available} available)
messages.reason.note_tag_missing: Tags in the source but not in the translation: {tags}
messages.reason.note_tag_extra: Tags in the translation but not in the source: {tags}
messages.reason.note_tag_missing_extra: Tags in the source but not in the translation: {missing} / tags in the translation but not in the source: {extra}
messages.reason.edit_no_header: There is no header row (the file is empty, or holds only comments and blank lines)
messages.reason.edit_bad_header: The header on line {line} is {text}, which is none of the four accepted forms (key,section,node,order,speaker,translation / key,speaker,translation / key,translation / key,section,node,order,speaker,source_en,translation)
messages.reason.edit_field_count: The field count does not match the header (the header has {header} columns, this row has {row})
messages.reason.edit_no_newline: A translation cannot contain a line break
messages.reason.edit_bad_utf8: The translation is not valid UTF-8
messages.reason.edit_multiline_translation: The translation contains a line break (a translation with line breaks cannot be changed from the screen yet)
messages.reason.edit_unclosed_quote: The quote opened on line {line} is never closed before the end of the file (everything after it becomes one value)
messages.reason.edit_cr_only: The file uses only CR as line breaks (the game reads the whole file as one line, so the screen does not write to it)
messages.reason.edit_swallow: Line {line} looks swallowed into this record's value (a quote may be closed in the wrong place)
messages.reason.edit_game_disagrees: The game's reader (CsvReader) reads the {column} column of this record differently
messages.reason.edit_game_misses_record: The game's reader (CsvReader) does not find this record
messages.reason.edit_no_key_or_source: The key column is neither a 16-digit key nor a line ID, and the source text (source_en) is empty (publish drops this record, so a translation written here is never published)
messages.reason.edit_recheck_failed: Reading back the record that starts on line {line} after rewriting it shows changes beyond the translation
messages.reason.publish_row_gone: This row is not in the new output
messages.reason.publish_translation_cleared: The new output leaves this row with an empty translation
messages.reason.publish_base_drift: The game has {count} different translations for {locale}
messages.reason.publish_no_key_column: The header has neither a key column nor a source_en column, so no row can get a key and every row is dropped
messages.reason.publish_no_translation_column: The header has no translation column, so every row is read as untranslated
messages.reason.publish_hash_header: The first column name of the header starts with '#'. The upstream tools/hash-strings.ps1 skips this header and takes the next line as the header, so it publishes no translation from this file
messages.reason.publish_rows_unread: The file has non-empty lines, yet not a single row can be read. Its lines are separated by something other than LF, CRLF or CR
messages.reason.publish_unclosed_quote: A quote is opened and never closed before the end of the file. Read as a whole, everything after it becomes one value
messages.reason.publish_swallow_key_shaped: Line {line}, read on its own, looks like a row that starts with a key. A quote seems to be closed in the wrong place, swallowing the lines after it into a value
messages.reason.publish_swallow_same_columns: Line {line}, read on its own, looks like a row with as many columns as the header. A quote seems to be closed in the wrong place, swallowing the lines after it into a value
messages.reason.publish_swallow_text_after_quote: On line {line}, a quoted value that spans lines is closed and text follows right after the closing quote. A quote seems to be closed in the wrong place, swallowing the lines after it into a value
messages.reason.publish_lone_cr: The {column} value contains a lone CR (a CR not followed by LF). The upstream tools/hash-strings.ps1 drops this row
messages.reason.publish_cr_cut: An unquoted value is cut by a lone CR at the end of the line, and its rest on line {line} is read as another row. The game drops the CR and reads them as one
messages.reason.publish_order_line_break: The {column} value contains a line break. publish writes this value as is, without quotes, so what follows the line break is read as another line next time
